From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Private hostname handoff & TLS delegation — action grid

Hi Alice / Acme security team,

Thanks again for the sync today. Per our architecture review, I’m attaching a concise handoff grid that maps private-hostname ownership to TLS termination and trust-anchor responsibilities for the on-prem/VPC deployment. The goal: a clear, operationalizable decision tree your infra team can sign off on so we can finish the private deployment runbook and start cert provisioning.

Quick asks:
- Please indicate which delegation tier you prefer for each FQDN listed in the spreadsheet (column: "Preferred Tier").
- Confirm whether Acme will provide a customer-managed CA cert (DER/PEM) or if you want Redwood to manage an intermediate for the private endpoints.
- Tell us the desired OCSP/CRL behavior — stapling from your edge, or Redwood-managed stapling on fallback proxy.

Notes about the grid (attached):
- Tier A (customer-edge TLS): customer controls private CA and certificates; Redwood verifies via pinned trust-anchor; DNS delegated to customer (NS delegation for private zone).
- Tier B (split-horizon CNAME -> rwd-private-proxy): DNS resolution depends on VPC peering; SNI routing to customer origin where present, with automatic fallback to proxy when origin unreachable.
- Tier C (Redwood-managed): wildcard for private namespace issued to Redwood-managed CA; strict MTLS optional for sensitive routes.

Attachments: private-hostname-handoff-grid.xlsx (spreadsheet with FQDN rows + columns for delegation, CA owner, OCSP, rotation window), mtls-guidance-playbook.pdf (playbook excerpt).

PTA: If you can mark the grid by EOD Friday (your timezone) we’ll schedule a short run-through with Aditya and Karthik to lock the cert rotation automation and DNS cutover windows.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Private hostname handoff & TLS delegation — action grid

Naomi, thanks — helpful summary and clean spreadsheet. We discussed two main operational preferences internally:

1) For customer-facing private hosts that terminate user traffic inside Acme networks, we prefer Tier A (customer-edge TLS) with our internal PKI.
2) For internal-only endpoints used by batch/async services across VPCs, we want Tier B for split-horizon CNAMEs pointing to the Redwood private proxy, with an automatic fallback in case of cross-region routing failures.

A couple of clarifying points:
- For Tier A, we will supply a trust-anchor bundle and an OCSP responder URL. We expect Redwood to pin that bundle with a 1:1 mapping per customer namespace.
- For Tier B fallback, we want the proxy to use OCSP stapling and to prefer customer origin certs when available. If Redwood must serve certs, we need to discuss proof-of-possession for private keys (HSM/KMS integration) and an SLA for rotation.

Timeline: we can return the annotated grid by Monday EOD. Also, procurement will request a short MSA addendum for TLS key custody — I’ll loop procurement if/when needed.

Naomi, Karthik — draft plan below (high level). I’ve attached a one-page automation sketch and a sample cert rotation calendar.

Key decisions proposed:
- Delegation grid: implement a 3-tier model (naming changed slightly from spreadsheet for clarity):
  * Tier 1 — Customer-managed CA + DNS NS delegation (Full customer ownership). Rotation cadence: 90 days recommended; Redwood will accept a trust-anchor bundle and validate via OCSP and TLS probe.
  * Tier 2 — Split-horizon CNAME -> rwd-private-proxy (Customer DNS uses on-prem views, public/private split via DNS views). Rotation cadence: 60 days for edge-origin certs; proxy certs managed by Redwood on a 30-day rotation when acting as fallback.
  * Tier 3 — Redwood-managed wildcard for private namespace (only for customers who opt-in). Rotation cadence: 30 days with HSM-backed private keys and automated renewal.

- OCSP/Stapling: prefer customer OCSP responder when Tier 1 is used. For Tier 2 fallback, proxy will staple OCSP from Redwood CA. We’ll implement short-lived stapled responses and a healthcheck that compares OCSP status between origin and proxy.

- Proof-of-possession & key custody: when Acme wants Redwood to sign/serve certs, require KMS/HSM integration (customer-managed keys preferred). For our internal managed certs we’ll store keys in Redwood HSM and expose limited rotation endpoints.

- DNS playbook highlights for Tier 2:
  1) Customer creates CNAME private.example.acme -> rwd-private-proxy.acme.rwd
  2) In on-prem bind/Route53 private zone, ensure split-horizon views resolve to the correct VPC addresses; validate via dig + EDNS.
  3) During cutover, switch TTLs to 60s; monitor metrics for 15 minutes and then increase to 300s.

- Rollout phases:
  1) Test harness (staging) with synthetic traffic + OCSP failure injection.
  2) Canary (one service namespace).
  3) Gradual expansion (by region).

- Emergency rotation: automated revocation and replacement script that rotates certs and updates stapling cache within 90s after private key compromise detection.

Attachments: mtls-guidance-playbook.pdf, private-hostname-handoff-grid.xlsx, cert-rotation-calendar.csv

I’ll prepare the 1-pager and runbook for the Wed call. Let me know if Acme requires any custom audit logging fields for their security team — we can add token-level TLS handshake logs to the Console retention for the account.
